knowledge:
- key_parameters: database=A database of gated cytometries built using buildDatabase ;; templates.number=The number of clusters/templates to look for in optimalFlowTemplates ;; consensus.method=The method used to obtain the template cytometry (e.g., "pooling", "k-barycenter", or "hierarchical") ;; classif.method=The supervised classification method used in optimalFlowClassification (e.g., QDA by default, "matching" for label-transfer, or "random forest") ;; cost.function=The cost function used when classif.method is "matching" (e.g., "ellipses") ;; cl.paral=Integer indicating parallel processing configuration
- alternatives: tclust is used internally as a robust extension of k-means for gating new cytometries ;; consensus.method options include "pooling" (default), "k-barycenter" (Wasserstein space barycenters), and "hierarchical" (density-based hdbscan, which automatically selects the number of cell types) ;; classif.method options include default QDA, "matching" (label-transfer), and "random forest"
- when_to_use: Use when you have a database of gated flow cytometry samples and want to perform supervised gating/classification on new, ungated cytometries, or when you want to group similar cytometries to identify common clinical conditions or diseases.
- pitfalls: When using consensus methods other than "pooling", cell types must be assigned to template clusters by voting, which often results in fuzzy classifications that must be converted to hard clusterings using f1ScoreVoting before evaluation ;; If weights do not add to 1 during classification, a normalization warning is triggered and applied.

workflows.name: template_generation_and_clustering
workflows.intent: Cluster a database of gated cytometries and generate representative prototype (template) cytometries.
input: database (a database of gated cytometries built from gated cytometry datasets)
workflows.stages: 1. Build the database of gated cytometries using buildDatabase ;; 2. Generate templates and cluster the database using optimalFlowTemplates ;; 3. Visualize the database clusters and templates using cytoPlotDatabase and cytoPlot.
workflows.code:
database <- buildDatabase(
 dataset_names = paste0('Cytometry', c(2:5, 7:9, 12:17, 19, 21)),
   population_ids = c('Monocytes', 'CD4+CD8-', 'Mature SIg Kappa', 'TCRgd-'))
templates.optimalFlow <-
  optimalFlowTemplates(
    database = database, templates.number = 5, cl.paral = 1
    )
cytoPlotDatabase(templates.optimalFlow$database.elliptical[which(templates.optimalFlow$clustering == 3)], dimensions = c(4,3), xlim = c(0, 8000), ylim = c(0, 8000), xlab = "", ylab = "")
cytoPlot(templates.optimalFlow$templates[[3]], dimensions = c(4,3), xlim = c(0, 8000), ylim = c(0, 8000), xlab = "", ylab = "")
templates.optimalFlow.barycenter <- 
  optimalFlowTemplates(
    database = database, templates.number = 5, consensus.method = "k-barycenter",
    barycenters.number = 4, bar.repetitions = 10, alpha.bar = 0.05, cl.paral = 1
    )
templates.optimalFlow.hdbscan <- 
  optimalFlowTemplates(
    database = database, templates.number = 5, consensus.method = "hierarchical",
    cl.paral = 1
    )
templates.optimalFlow.unsup <-
  optimalFlowTemplates(
    database = database, hclust.method = "hdbscan", cl.paral = 1, consensus.method = "hierarchical"
    )

workflows.name: supervised_cytometry_classification
workflows.intent: Classify and gate a new, ungated cytometry using a database of gated cytometries and pre-computed templates.
input: templates.optimalFlow (the templates object generated by optimalFlowTemplates)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare the test cytometry by selecting relevant marker columns ;; 2. Perform supervised classification using optimalFlowClassification with the chosen consensus and classification methods ;; 3. Evaluate classification performance using f1Score or f1ScoreVoting.
workflows.code:
test.cytometry <- Cytometry1[which(match(Cytometry1$`Population ID (name)`, c("Monocytes", "CD4+CD8-", "Mature SIg Kappa", "TCRgd-"), nomatch = 0) > 0), ]
classification.optimalFlow <- 
  optimalFlowClassification(
    test.cytometry[, 1:10], database, templates.optimalFlow, 
    consensus.method = "pooling", cl.paral = 1
    )
scoreF1.optimalFlow <- optimalFlow::f1Score(classification.optimalFlow$cluster,
                                            test.cytometry, noise.types)
classification.optimalFlow.barycenter <-
  optimalFlowClassification(
    test.cytometry[, 1:10],
    database, templates.optimalFlow.barycenter, consensus.method = "k-barycenter", cl.paral = 1
    )
scoreF1.optimalFlow.barycenter <- 
  f1ScoreVoting(
    classification.optimalFlow.barycenter$cluster.vote, classification.optimalFlow.barycenter$cluster,
    test.cytometry,
    1.01, noise.types
    )
classification.optimalFlow.hdbscan <-
  optimalFlowClassification(
    test.cytometry[, 1:10],
    database, templates.optimalFlow.hdbscan, consensus.method = "hierarchical", cl.paral = 1
    )
classification.optimalFlow.2 <-
  optimalFlowClassification(
    test.cytometry[, 1:10],
    database, templates.optimalFlow, consensus.method = "pooling", classif.method = "matching",
    cost.function = "ellipses", cl.paral = 1
    )
classification.optimalFlow.3 <-
  optimalFlowClassification(
    test.cytometry[, 1:10],
    database, templates.optimalFlow, consensus.method = "pooling",
    classif.method = "random forest", cl.paral = 1
    )
